title: Urgent Escalation Handoff and SLA Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational steps, artifact requirements, and communication templates for urgent escalations affecting enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). It standardizes handoff from Support -> Customer Success -> Engineering/SRE/On‑Prem teams and ensures SLA alignment, rapid mitigation, and consistent post‑mortem follow-through.

Scope: Applies to incidents triggered by customer-facing outages, severe quality regressions, billing anomalies tied to inference, or security-sensitive events that impact an enterprise account. Not intended for routine tickets or feature requests.

Audience: Support L2/L3, Customer Success Managers (CSM), Solutions Engineers (SE), SRE/Runtime Engineers, Dedicated/Private deployment owners.

Problem statement: Enterprise customers expect predictable SLAs and clear escalation paths. During multiteam incidents we observe delays due to missing telemetry, unclear ownership for Dedicated/Private handoffs, and inconsistent customer comms. This playbook remedies those gaps.

---

Severity definitions and SLA targets

1) Severity taxonomy (enterprise standard)
   - Sev1 (Critical): Complete or near-complete service unavailability for production traffic (e.g., 100% request failures, model serve crash, data exfiltration).
   - Sev2 (High): Severe degradation impacting a large subset of traffic or major feature (e.g., P95 latency > 5x SLO, repeat hallucination producing sensitive output).
   - Sev3 (Medium): Partial loss of functionality or reduced performance affecting a minority of users; workaround exists.
   - Sev4 (Low): Minor issues, documentation questions, enhancement requests.

2) SLA targets (enterprise response/acknowledge + mitigation expectations)
   - Sev1: Acknowledge within 15 minutes. Initial mitigation plan within 60 minutes. Customer update every 30 minutes until mitigation. Target full resolution or acceptable workaround in 6 hours (unless constrained by on‑prem factors).
   - Sev2: Acknowledge within 60 minutes. Plan within 4 business hours. Updates every 2–4 hours. Target resolution in 2 business days.
   - Sev3: Acknowledge within 1 business day. Resolution in the next scheduled release or 10 business days depending on root cause.
   - Sev4: Acknowledge in 3 business days. Standard backlog handling.

Note: SLA windows for Dedicated/Private include an additional coordination layer (customer network access/maintenance windows) — see Handoff constraints.

---

Initial triage checklist (Support L2) — required within first 15 minutes for Sev1 or 60 minutes for Sev2

1) Collect required artifacts (attach to ticket and PagerDuty incident):
   - Customer account ID and Org name.
   - Endpoint / route / deployment ID.
   - Model name + pinned version + quantization profile.
   - Timestamped example request and response (redact PII if present).
   - Correlation ID / request_id(s) and approximate client-side timestamps.
   - Error messages, stack traces, HTTP status codes, and any gateway logs.
   - Last successful invocation timestamp and recent deployment/rollout history.
   - Telemetry: P95/P99 latency, error rate, tokens per request, GPU utilization, queue depth for the affected pool, KV-cache hit rate.
   - Billing anomaly snapshot if cost-related (token counts, cost per token, sudden spike windows).

2) Quick checks (yes/no, mark in ticket):
   - Has customer performed any recent config changes, model pin/rollback, or prompt changes?
   - Is the problem reproducible from a Redwood test account? (If yes, include test case.)
   - Are all upstream dependencies healthy (KMS, networking, storage)?

3) Escalate to CSM and SE immediately for enterprise accounts. If Sev1, trigger PagerDuty on the on-call SRE and schedule an ad‑hoc war room Slack channel using the naming convention: #incident-<org>-<YYYYMMDD>-sevx

---

Handoff rules: Support -> Customer Success -> Engineering/SRE/Private Deployment Owners

Required before handing to engineering (pre-handoff gate):
   - Ticket contains the artifact checklist above. Tickets missing artifacts should be blocked and returned to Support for completion.
   - Customer impact statement: exact percentage of traffic affected and business impact (e.g., checkout failures, revenue impact).
   - Existing mitigations attempted (rolling restart, retry config changes, temporary routing).

Handoff steps (numbered):
   1. Support creates or updates the PagerDuty incident and attaches the artifact checklist.
   2. Support posts the initial summary to the incident Slack channel using the template below and @mentions on‑call SRE and the SE.
   3. CSM joins and validates customer impact and expectations (maintenance windows, acceptable rollback).
   4. SE/Engineer reviews artifacts within SLA windows and responds with assigned owner, triage hypothesis, and next steps.
   5. If Dedicated/Private deployment is involved, contact the dedicated deployment owner and confirm remote access, scheduled maintenance windows, and KMS/HSM availability.

Access & permissions check (for Private/Dedicated):
   - Confirm support SSH bastion or SSM access exists to the customer appliance or private control plane.
   - Confirm service account roles and KMS key access are present for debug actions.
   - Confirm network ACLs allow control-plane callbacks or metrics scraping.

---

Mitigation patterns and temporary fixes (SRE/Runtime):

Common quick mitigations (ordered by risk):
   - Route traffic to a fallback model variant with compatible API surface (example: model-v2 -> model-v1-fallback).
   - Increase autoscale pool size for Dedicated temporarily (documented approval required for > 2x baseline).
   - Apply rate limiting at the customer route to protect shared capacity while retaining critical flows.
   - Disable affected feature flags or re-enable previous rollout hold.
   - Perform targeted rollback to last-known-good model version or quantization profile.

Commands and steps (examples)
   - Check running pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l deployment=<deployment-id> --context=<cluster>
   - Restart gateway: systemctl restart redwood-gateway or restart deployment via orchestration console
   - Roll back model: redact CLI example to ensure correct cadence: rwctl deploy rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <sha>

Safety notes: Always capture hashes and export model artifacts before any destructive change. For Private deployments, coordinate snapshot creation with the customer's ops lead.

---

Communication templates (copy-and-send)

Slack initial incident post (paste into #incident-...):

"<INCIDENT SUMMARY>
Severity: <Sev1|Sev2>
Customer: <Org name> (Account ID: <id>)
Impact: <short statement e.g., 80% of production calls failing; checkout flow blocked>
First seen: <ISO timestamp>
Affected endpoints: <route ids>
Artifacts attached: example request/response, logs, metrics snapshot, deployment history
Assigned: @oncall-sre @se-owner @csm-<org>
Next step: <hypothesis or action>"

Email update subject line (to customer):
   [ACTION REQUIRED] Incident <INCIDENT-ID> — <Short impact> — Redwood Inference status and next steps

Email body (initial):
   Short summary, what we know, what we're doing, expected next update cadence, and a single POC contact (CSM). Attach the incident link and support ticket.

Customer update cadence examples:
   - Sev1: 30-minute cadence until mitigated.
   - Sev2: 2–4 hour cadence until stabilised.

---

PagerDuty and on-call routing guidance

Suggested policy:
   - PagerDuty escalation: Support L2 -> SRE on-call -> Runtime engineer -> Platform lead.
   - For Dedicated/Private critical incidents, add the Dedicated Deployment on-call rotation as an escalation step.
   - If incident remains unresolved after 3 hours with customer impact, escalation to Director-level (CS and Engineering Directors) required.

On-call runbook excerpt (short):
   - Step 0: Acknowledge incident.
   - Step 1: Verify artifacts present.
   - Step 2: Assign pairing engineer and open console/war room.
   - Step 3: Identify whether mitigation is routing/scale/rollback.
   - Step 4: Execute mitigation with a single operator performing change and another observing / capturing logs.

---

Dedicated & Private deployment-specific considerations

Constraints often encountered:
   - Customer network maintenance windows prevent immediate access.
   - KMS/HSM approval gating prevents key rotation or model loads.
   - On‑prem hardware nodes may require physical intervention or vendor escalation.

Handoff checklist additions for Private/Dedicated:
   - Network topology diagram and bastion credentials (or ticket to request access).
   - Onsite maintenance window preferences and escalation phone numbers.
   - Location of on‑prem runbooks and vendor SLAs.
   - Customer technical contact and on‑call schedule.

Recommended temporary fallback prioritization: Hosted fallbacks first (if allowed by contract), then Dedicated pool scaling, then Private local mitigations.

---

Required telemetry & dashboards (for incident and postmortem)

Minimum charts to capture at the start of incident:
   - P95 and P99 request latency for affected route and global.
   - Error rate (5-minute and 1-hour windows) and error breakdown by HTTP status / internal error class.
   - GPU utilization per node, queue depth, and model KV cache hit rate.
   - Token throughput (tokens/sec), average tokens per invocation.
   - Autoscaler actions (recent scale events) and pod restart counts.
   - Billing token spikes correlated to timestamps.

Retention: snapshot of 72 hours around incident saved to incident artifacts storage.

---

Post-incident process & QBR inclusion

1) Immediate post-incident (within 24 hours):
   - Incident timeline and responsible owners posted to ticket.
   - Customer-facing summary drafted by CSM and approved by engineering for accuracy.
   - Short-term mitigations documented and follow-up tickets created for permanent fixes.

2) Root cause analysis (within 5 business days):
   - Full timeline, contributing factors, and a 3-point corrective action plan (short, medium, long term).
   - Identify whether regression was caused by model change, infra, config, or customer behavior.
   - Assign owners and target dates for remediation.

3) QBR / Health Check inclusion (next scheduled QBR):
   - Include incident summary, customer impact metrics, remediation status, and CSAT follow-up.
   - Present changes to SLOs or operational controls if required (e.g., new routing policies, additional observability).

4) Severity reclassification and SLA reconciliation:
   - Confirm final severity (may be downgraded after RCA).
   - Reconcile any SLA credits or contractual obligations with Finance and Legal.

---

RACI cheat sheet (flat table)

| Activity | Support L2 | CSM | SE/Dev | SRE/Runtime | Dedicated/Private Owner | Director/Leadership |
|---------|-----------:|-----:|-------:|-----------:|------------------------:|-------------------:|
| Initial triage and artifact collection | R | A | C | C | C | I |
| PagerDuty incident creation | R | I | C | A | C | I |
| Customer communications | C | R | I | I | I | I |
| Temporary mitigation (rollback/route) | I | I | C | A | R | I |
| Postmortem and RCA | I | R | C | A | C | I |

Legend: R = Responsible, A = Accountable, C = Consulted, I = Informed

---

Checklist for handoff artifacts (consolidated)

- [ ] Customer account ID & contact list
- [ ] Sample request/response with correlation IDs
- [ ] Exact error messages and deployment change history
- [ ] Live metrics snapshot (P95/P99 latency, error rate)
- [ ] Billing/cost spike evidence (if applicable)
- [ ] Access checklist for Dedicated/Private (bastion, KMS access)
- [ ] Customer impact statement and allowable mitigation window

---

Training & run frequency

- Run an enterprise escalation tabletop at least quarterly with SRE, Support, and CSM teams.
- Maintain a living incident playbook with retrospective updates post each Sev1/Sev2.
- Update dedicated/private access lists quarterly or after every major customer onboarding.

---

Appendix: Useful snippets and links

- PagerDuty runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall/pagerduty-escalation-policy
- Incident template (Jira): /confluence/eng-platform/templates/incident-template
- Dedicated deployment owner roster: internal roster (CSM shared drive)
- Example rollback command (CLI): rwctl deploy rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <sha>

If you are missing any required artifact, do not proceed with engineering handoff — return the ticket to Support L2 with the missing fields explicitly listed.

Contact matrix for urgent escalation (primary):
   - Support lead on-call: @support-oncall (PagerDuty)
   - SRE on-call: @sre-oncall (PagerDuty)
   - CSM for enterprise accounts: see account roster (CS shared drive)
   - SE owner: per-customer mapping in account record

End of playbook.
